intents.text: Add starlette/middleware/body_limit.py with a pure ASGI RequestBodyLimitMiddleware(app, max_body_size: int) that wraps receive, counts the body bytes actually received (including multipart file data and encoding overhead), and answers with a plain-text 413 Content Too Large when the total exceeds max_body_size.

Use Content-Length only as a fail-fast check: a declared length above the limit is rejected before the body is read, while an absent or understated header never bypasses the byte-count limit, and a body exactly at the limit is allowed.
If the application has already started sending a response when the limit is crossed, the middleware sends no second response but the receive stream is still stopped by the body-limit error.
Add a keyword max_body_size: int | None = None to Starlette, Router, Mount and Route, where None keeps today's unlimited behaviour.

Apply the application-level limit through the middleware stack before routing (so application middleware that reads the body is subject to it), and let a limit on an inner route, mount or router override the outer one after routing, both raising and lowering it.
In starlette/formparsers.py, close any temporary files the multipart parser created whenever a parse is interrupted for any reason, including a body-limit error raised mid-stream.
Export nothing new at the package root; the middleware is imported only from starlette.middleware.body_limit.

Add tests for the middleware (limit with and without Content-Length, understated Content-Length, exactly-at-limit, multipart uploads, streaming bodies, no double response), for max_body_size on Starlette, Router, Mount and Route including inner limits raising and lowering the outer one, and for multipart temp-file cleanup, keeping the existing suite green.

constraints: Do not change unrelated behaviour; the existing test suite must stay green.
Default max_body_size=None must preserve current unlimited behaviour.
Do not export anything new from the starlette package root.
The middleware must be pure ASGI (not BaseHTTPMiddleware).
